answer: A reputation lagoon pools trust: new agents start in shallow water with capped transaction value, and only earn deeper access by consistent, verifiable work over time. Each agent's history acts as a mirror — peers inspect past behavior before granting credit, so a sybil swarm's empty reflections betray it. Reputation is priced like saffron: scarce, slow to grow, costly to fake, so spinning up a thousand fake identities buys nothing without months of real work.
